newsitem.title: USA: USDA official optimistic before talks in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: USDA official optimistic before talks in Turkey.

text.p: An Agriculture Department official said Friday he was fairly optimistic that a lingering dispute that has delayed U.S. grain shipments to Turkey can be resolved next week in a meeting in Turkey between U.S. and Turkish officials.

Commenting shortly before departing Washington for Turkey, Jonathan Jones, national export program manager for USDA's Animal Plant and Health Inspection Service, said Washington was notified by Turkey's Ministery of Agriculture late Thursday that Turkey is putting together a council of experts to study the issues and consider the necessary revisions that would be in concert with international standards.
Jones said this was an important and positive development, and would hopefully pave the way towards resolution of the problem.
"This indicates a desire to be in line with what the rest of the world is doing, and this is an important first step," Jones said. "It looks better than it did a few days ago."
Jones and Roy Barrett, marketing specialist with USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service, will meet Turkish plant protection officials in Ankara the first of next week.

U.S. grain shipments to Turkey have been held up for weeks due to a disagreement over Turkey's strict import regulations. U.S. officials contend that Turkey's regulations are too strict and do not fit with other international stanadards. The USDA has stopped issuing any phytosanitary certificates for all grains and oilseed shipments to Turkey until the issue is settled.
Jones said earlier this week that there are currently three ships of U.S. wheat totalling 85,000 tonnes waiting to be unloaded in Turkish ports.
